title: Laboratory Microbiology and PCR Technician - Hagyard Equine Medical Insitute
description:
PetVet Care Centers' Hagyard Equine Medical Institute is currently seeking a Laboratory Microbiology and PCR Technician to join their team!

At PetVet Care Centers, our mission is to improve the lives of animals and people — providing exceptional and compassionate care at every stage — for all the moments that matter.

Because life is better with pets.

We deliver the Ultimate Care Experience — every pet, every client, every time. That starts with a Culture of Care that supports our team members as much as the pets and clients we serve.

With more than 420 locally led hospitals and over 11,000 team members nationwide, we offer:

  • Local autonomy with national support
  • Career mobility and development opportunities
  • A collaborative, inclusive environment where your wellbeing comes first

You care for pets. We care for you.

Position Overview

Position: Laboratory Microbiology and PCR Technician, Medical Technologist - Generalist

Location: Hagyard Laboratory

Reports to: Lab Manager

Essential Duties and Responsibilities include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

  • Perform laboratory analysis of specimens from all patients in the clinical areas of hematology, chemistry, coagulation, microbiology, and special tests using established protocol and Quality control checks.
  • Provide support to all areas within the laboratory including chemistry, hematology, endocrinology, Coggins, microbiology, and administrative functions.
  • Report results as required adhering to established techniques and guidelines.
  • Perform daily quality control on automated equipment to assure high quality of performance.
  • Assist with preventative maintenance guidelines as directed to ensure proper function and efficiency of lab equipment and instruments.
  • Report inventory and laboratory material and supply shortages to appropriate department heads and order only as directed.
  • Restock supplies and tools in all areas as needed daily.
  • Assist in orienting and training new employees with job responsibilities and techniques.
  • Provide theoretical and technical information to other laboratory personnel, techs, or veterinarians regarding laboratory data and technical requirements.
  • Adhere to hospital and laboratory policies, procedures, objectives, and quality assurance programs.
  • Maintain efficient and clean workspaces adhering to OSHA guidelines and laboratory policies.
  • Attend meetings as required and participate in external industry related functions as directed.
  • Enhance professional growth through participation in educational workshops, reading current literature, and attending educational programs.
  • Complete and contribute to special projects as assigned.

Hematology

  • Process patient specimens utilizing the hematology analyzer. Identify any instrument errors, troubleshoot, and communicate with approved service providers as needed to resolve equipment problems.
  • Read and interpret abnormal white blood cell counts utilizing the microscope.
  • Process fluid analysis specimens and cytology specimens efficiently and accurately.
  • Process fibrinogen request as directed in per the laboratory procedure manual.
  • Run urinalysis as directed in procedure manual.
  • Process NI Screen’s, JFA’s, and cross matches as directed in procedure manual.

Chemistry

  • Process patient specimens utilizing the chemistry analyzer. Identify any instrument errors, troubleshoot, and communicate with approved service providers as needed to resolve equipment problems.
  • Run specialized chemistry tests: i.e.: Ammonia, Triglycerides, running controls as outlined in the procedure manual prior to processing the specimen.
  • Run blood gases, ionized calcium, SAA, PT and PTT specimens as outlined in the laboratory procedures.
  • Restock and formulate reagents as needed and adhering to laboratory guidelines.

Endocrinology & Coggins

  • Prepare reagents and perform endocrinology testing including Progesterones, T4, and PMSG utilizing the TOSOH as needed.
  • Prepare, set up and interpret results of Coggins samples according to federal USDA guidelines (Requires federal certification).
  • Federal certification of Coggins will require an employee to either do on-line training or be sent to NVSL for Coggins training. Hagyard’s will pay for training, in return for 2 years of service.

Microbiology

  • Prepare and plate all specimens as directed in the laboratory procedure manual in an efficient and timely manner.
  • Process kit tests for Rotavirus, Clostridium difficile toxin and Clostridium perfringens Enterotoxin samples.
  • Process, read and report fecal egg counts.
  • Report significant findings to appropriate veterinarian and infectious disease officer as directed.
  • Restock primary bench daily.

Administrative Responsibilities

  • Provide telephone and reception report to lab administrative throughout shifts.
  • Record receipt of specimen and create accurate lab requisitions properly labeling and distributing specimens to required departments for timely processing.
  • Follow up and investigate incomplete specimen information as needed.
  • Assist clients and visitors with questions and issues, referring significant issues to department head and lab supervisor.
  • Prepare external/send out specimens to be performed at a reference lab completing proper forms and packaging as necessary following federal shipping requirements.

Miscellaneous Responsibilities

  • Process STAT tests, critical specimens, and emergency requests as directed.
  • Review and sign laboratory procedure manuals in all areas at least once annually ensuring knowledge of updated procedures and policies

Expectations

  • Display a positive image of HDM by demonstrating courteous and professional behavior toward clients, veterinarians, visitors, interns, technicians, and other employees
  • To treat other people with respect and consideration regardless of their status or position.
  • To be dependable and punctual on working hours scheduled and to be willing to stay beyond scheduled hours if needed.
  • To assist in achieving and maintaining high quality standards in the overall services provided to clients and doctors.
  • To be a self-starter and take the required initiative to perform all tasks successfully.
  • To maintain confidentiality with regards to client-patient rights.
  • To conduct oneself professionally as a representative of Hagyard Equine Medical Institute refraining from inappropriate language and behavior.
  • To constructively communicate progress, problems or other issues requiring attention to the appropriate doctor or member of management.
  • To foster teamwork by working with area members to find solutions to problems or needs regarding clients, patient care, operational needs, and the working environment.
  • To identify ways to motivate and encourage area members.
  • To offer solutions and demonstrate a positive attitude when dealing with clients, doctors, management, staff members, and outside vendors or suppliers.
  • To give guidance to other personnel in understanding the importance of adhering to procedures and proper protocol.
  • To maintain a professional appearance and a courteous attitude.
  • To maintain a clean/sanitary and well-organized work/service area at all times.

Performance Abilities

  • Professional demeanor
  • Respects confidentiality of client/patient data.
  • Strong oral communication skills.
  • Strong customer service skills.
  • Strong computer skills.
  • Detail oriented and able to take directions.
  • Organized, dedicated, friendly and responsible.
  • Punctual and low absenteeism.

Qualifications

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Applicants must be 18 years of age or older to be considered for this position
  • Education/Experience/Certificates:
    • Must be a Medical Technologist (MT, ASCP certified or AMT), Medical Laboratory Technician (MLT, ASCP certified or AMT) or equivalent (adequate on the job training).
    • Previous equine/animal laboratory experience is preferred
  • Language Ability:
    • Ability to read, analyze, and interpret general technical procedures. Ability to write/document technical information and general correspondence. Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from doctors, other staff and clients.
  • Math Ability:
    • Ability to apply intermediate math formulas.
  • Reasoning Ability:
    • Ability to apply common sense understanding to carry out instructions furnished in written, oral, or diagram form. Ability to deal with problems involving several concrete variables in standardized situations.
  • Computer Skills:
    • To perform this job successfully, an individual should have general computer software knowledge and keyboarding skills.
  • Work Environment:
    • The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
      • May be exposed to fumes or airborne particles;
      • May be exposed to toxic or caustic chemicals
      • Regularly works near moving mechanical parts.
  • Physical Demands
    • The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
    • While performing the duties of this Job, the employee is:
      • Ability to life more than 30lbs
      • Frequently (approximately 90% of the daily work) required to use arms, hands and fingers for computer work.
      • Frequently required to talk and hear while communicating in person and via the telephone,
      • Frequently required to stand for long periods of time,
      • Occasionally required to sit or walk.
    • Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus to be able to accurately interpret of kit tests, slides and specimens via the microscope.

Schedule

  • The Hagyard Laboratory is open Monday through Sunday, 6AM through 9PM during peak season (February - June). During off season (July - January) the laboratory is open Monday through Friday 7AM through 5PM, Saturday 7AM through 2PM, and Sunday 7AM through 12PM.
  • This position is primarily first shift, with an understanding hours may shift slightly during the peak season. Weekend availability will be required, but will rotate.
  • Schedule can be four 10-hour shifts, or five 8-hour shifts.

What We Offer
We care deeply about supporting our team members — professionally and personally. Benefits include:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Paid Parental Leave (birth, adoption, foster)
  • 401(k) with discretionary contribution
  • Team Member Pet Discounts
  • Emotional wellbeing support — including Calm app access and 24/7 EAP
  • CE stipends and career development resources
  • Grant Circle — a relief fund for team members facing personal hardship
  • Local hospital culture backed by national resources
Pay Range
$22—$33 USD

At PetVet Care Centers, we’re committed to a Culture of Care — for pets, for the people who love them, and for the team members who make it all possible. With more than 400 hospitals across the U.S. and a team of over 11,000 dedicated professionals, including 1700+ veterinarians, we offer a unique blend of local leadership and national support that helps our hospitals thrive.

Our model is built on partnership, collaboration, and local medical autonomy, empowering each hospital to deliver high-quality care while benefiting from shared resources and a strong professional community. Whether you’re providing care in a hospital or supporting operations behind the scenes, PetVet is a place where you can grow your career, stay connected to your purpose, and make a meaningful impact.

You care for pets. We care for you.

All employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, age, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, marital status, pregnancy, religion, citizenship, national origin/ancestry, physical/mental disabilities, military status or any other basis prohibited by law. EOE, M/F/D/V

title: Thermal Engineer, Thermal Protection Systems (TPS)
description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

About the Team

The Thermal Engineering team enables Anduril's rapid hardware development cycle by ensuring advanced defense systems perform reliably in demanding real-world environments. The team works across high-power, tightly integrated products where thermal architecture, analysis, testing, and cross-functional design decisions directly affect product performance, reliability, and mission success.

About the Role

We are looking for a Thermal Engineer specializing in Thermal Protection Systems (TPS) to join our team. In this role, you will own the design, analysis, and validation of thermal protection for hypersonic and high-speed flight systems operating in extreme aerothermal environments.

This role is ideal for someone with deep expertise in aerothermal heating, ablative material response, and high-temperature thermal analysis — someone who can work across first-principles hand calculations, material response modeling, and detailed CFD to guide fast, high-consequence design decisions for systems where thermal survival is the critical constraint.

What You'll Do

  • Own TPS design, material selection, and thermal analysis for hypersonic and high-speed flight vehicles, including missiles, reentry systems, and advanced flight platforms.
  • Perform aerothermal heating analysis using engineering correlations, boundary-layer methods, and CFD to define the thermal environment across flight trajectories.
  • Conduct ablation and material response modeling to predict TPS recession, in-depth thermal response, and structural thermal margins under mission-representative conditions.
  • Evaluate and select TPS materials, including carbon phenolic, PICA, silicone-based ablators, ceramics, and high-temperature composites, based on aerothermal loads, mass constraints, and manufacturability.
  • Partner with aerodynamics, structures, propulsion, and systems engineers to integrate TPS into vehicle design while managing mass, volume, and performance tradeoffs.
  • Define and execute thermal and material characterization tests, including arcjet testing, furnace testing, and instrumented flight-article thermal testing.
  • Build and maintain thermal models spanning hand calculations through detailed FEA/CFD to predict system performance, establish design limits, and support qualification.
  • Present TPS status, risks, tradeoffs, and recommendations in internal design reviews and customer-facing technical reviews.
  • Support failure reviews and root-cause investigations using test data, thermal analysis, and first-principles reasoning.

Required Qualifications

  • MS or PhD in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Applied Physics, or a related field with a focus on aerothermodynamics, heat transfer, thermal sciences, or materials science.
  • 2+ years of experience in TPS design, aerothermal analysis, or high-temperature material response for aerospace or defense systems.
  • Strong first-principles understanding of aerodynamic heating, ablation, high-temperature heat transfer, and material thermal response.
  • Experience with material response modeling tools such as FIAT, CMA, TITAN, or equivalent ablation/thermal response codes.
  • Experience supporting thermal design for hypersonic vehicles, reentry systems, missiles, rocket nozzles, or other systems operating in extreme aerothermal environments.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Top Secret security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with aerothermal CFD tools such as DPLR, US3D, Loci-CHEM, CFD++, ANSYS Fluent, or STAR-CCM+ for high-speed reacting flow analysis.
  • Experience with arcjet testing, thermal characterization testing, or flight-article thermal instrumentation.
  • Experience with high-temperature materials including carbon phenolic, carbon-carbon, PICA, SLA-561V, silicone-based ablators, or ceramic matrix composites.
  • Experience with radiation modeling tools such as NEQAIR, HARA, or equivalent nonequilibrium radiation solvers.
  • Experience using MATLAB, Python, or similar tools for trajectory-based heating analysis, thermal margin assessment, or engineering trade studies.
  • Familiarity with NASA TPS heritage tools and databases (TPSX, CEA, CBAero).
  • Experience supporting PDR/CDR, qualification testing, or flight programs.
  • Strong motivation to support Anduril's mission of defending the United States and allied partners.
US Salary Range
$129,000—$171,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Benefits

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates.     • Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

  • What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. title: Senior Software Engineer
location: Denver, New York City, us, north_america
description:
Every person and every business connected to the Global Financial Internet. Built on Mural.

That's the world Mural is building. This role is one of the hands on the brush.

About Mural

Mural is regulated financial infrastructure across the US and Latin America. The whole stack, one partner. Companies build cross-border financial products on us using our API. We carry the licenses, the compliance, and the failure states, so they go live in weeks instead of months. Under the hood, fiat and blockchain run as one system. Their customers never see any of it. Money comes in, money goes out, and it just gets there.

We've processed over $2 billion across US dollar, stablecoin, and international rails. That includes USDC and USDT on major blockchains, ACH and wire in the US, and local rails across Latin America and Europe (PIX, SPEI, Bre-B, CBU/CVU, SEPA). Customers include Deel, Bolt, Opera, Koywe, Taxdome, Uniswap, Movii, and more. We recently closed our Series A. And we're an AI-native company. Agentic tools are how we build, operate, and scale.

The Role

You'll be joining a lean, high-intensity engineering team at an inflection point, processing billions in volume today. You'll work directly with our CTO, contributing full-stack from week one. The team is exceptional, with people from Palantir, McKinsey, DoorDash, Mercado Libre, Circle, and BlackRock, and we're only adding people who make it stronger.

This role is about three things.

1. Building Infrastructure That Moves Money

You'll work on the core systems that power global payments. State machines, transaction pipelines, reconciliation flows. Accuracy is non-negotiable when money is on the line, but so is the ability to build systems that adapt as the financial landscape evolves. You'll own features end-to-end, think carefully about failure modes, and write code you're proud to put your name on.

2. Shaping the Product

You're not just implementing tickets. You'll collaborate closely with our CTO, BD team, and directly with customers to evolve our API and platform, making complex financial flows feel intuitive for the developers and businesses building on top of us. If you see a better way to build something, you'll say so. If a tradeoff matters, you'll surface it. We want engineers who think like owners.

3. Setting the Bar

As an early engineering hire, you'll have an outsized influence on how we build. The patterns we establish, the standards we hold, the culture we cultivate. We believe quality engineering lives at the intersection of theory and experimentation. Think rigorously, ship decisively. You'll help define what that looks like in practice.

Who You Are

You're a strong individual contributor who works well across the full team. You don't need someone looking over your shoulder. You take ownership of your work end-to-end, communicate honestly about timelines and constraints, and never let something fall through the cracks because it wasn't technically "your problem."

You're comfortable with the full stack. You have at least 4+ years shipping production-grade infrastructure with Node and NestJS (or something comparable) and React with TypeScript. You're proficient building client facing APIs and asynchronous backend systems with complex state machines (event queuing, job scheduling, webhook delivery, failure recovery, and so on). You move fluidly between frontend and backend depending on what the problem requires. You care about design and have high standards for what you ship. Not just whether it works, but whether it feels right.

You're built for startups. You know what it means to operate in an environment with high ambiguity and real stakes. You move fast, make good decisions under uncertainty, and find energy in the challenge rather than frustration in the chaos. You've worked in a high-growth environment before, or you're deeply ready for one.

You're obsessed with correctness and resilience. Moving money globally means the margin for error is low. You think carefully about edge cases, error handling, and what happens when things go wrong, because they will. You love a good state machine. You appreciate systems that are both robust and easy to reason about.

You're curious about what we're building. You don't need to come from a fintech background, but you should be genuinely interested in stablecoins, global payments, and the financial infrastructure being rebuilt around them. The engineers who thrive here see the mission as part of the appeal, not just the tech stack.

What Success Looks Like

  • You're shipping meaningful features from week one, contributing to our platform and API with minimal ramp-up time

  • The systems you build are reliable, readable, and maintainable, with code that the team is proud of and that scales with us

  • You've raised the bar through the patterns you introduce, the reviews you give, and the standards you hold

  • You've become a key voice on engineering decisions, someone our CTO relies on when it matters

How We Work

We run on three principles.

2% better, every day. One percent for yourself, one percent for the people around you.

Telos. From the Greek word telos, meaning not just done but fulfilled. Everyone here is focused on one mission and knows each other's Telos.

Abundance. We can create anything we set our minds to, for ourselves, our partners, and our entire Mural family.

We're builders all the way down. Code is a medium, like paint. We choose honesty over polish and never claim what isn't true. We obsess over boring details, because trust is built in RFIs, refunds, and response times. And we hire for curiosity. It's a bar, not a poster.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Competitive cash base salary

  • Meaningful early-stage equity

  • Health insurance

  • 401(k)

  • Visa sponsorship available

Location

New York City or Denver, in person.

We named this company Mural because murals have always told the story of a community. They are made by hand, made together, painted onto the foundations of a place, and meant to outlast the people who started them. Every person who joins brings a new piece.

Now let's build a force of nature business, together.

title: Army - Project Manager (near Washington DC area)
description:
Company Overview:
Integrated Data Services (IDS) is a leading provider of custom software products and Government financial management services. IDS was founded in 1997 in El Segundo, CA, and since that time has seen tremendous growth and success. Currently, IDS has offices supporting customers nationwide. By providing customers with fast, efficient and reliable information systems and support services, IDS has become a preferred provider of financial and programmatic systems, services and solutions across a wide variety of government agencies.

Position Description:
Integrated Data Services (IDS) is seeking a Project Manager to lead the deployment and adoption of the Comprehensive Cost and Requirements (CCaR™) System across the Department of the Army to include the Army Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Organizations, and Subordinate Capability Program Executive (CPE) organizations. This operates at the intersection of financial management, enterprise software, and senior leader decision-making, directly enabling Army leadership to transition from static, manual processes to real-time, data-driven decision advantage. This is a mission-critical leadership role responsible for standing up the Army’s next-generation Program-to-Budget-to-Execution Data Integration and Workflow Solution. The selected candidate will directly shape how the Army executes budget and execution decisions, replacing static, manual processes with real-time, data-driven decision advantage.

The Army Project Manager will serve as the primary contractor interface with the AAS Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR), the ASA-ALT Technical Point of Contact (TPOC), and all authorized Government stakeholders and program authorities. This individual will ensure disciplined execution of approved plans, schedules, and governance processes while maintaining real-time visibility into cost, schedule, performance, and risk. This individual will engage directly with senior Army leadership, including resource sponsors and FM stakeholders.

This is a high-visibility role requiring a blend of operational program management, customer engagement, and cross-functional team leadership. The ideal candidate brings a minimum of ten (10) years of Department of the Army (DoA) program management experience, an active PMP or PgMP certification, comprehensive knowledge of the PPBE process, and hands-on experience with defense business and accounting systems such as GFEBS. This role is central to enabling the Army’s transition to real-time, data-driven decision advantage by ensuring the CCaR™ deployment is executed with precision, accountability, and full stakeholder alignment.

Worksite Location:
We are ideally seeking a candidate based in the Washington, DC/DMV area. This position is currently remote; however, onsite support at a government or customer location may be required in the future. The candidate must be willing and able to support onsite requirements as they arise on an as needed basis.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Program Leadership & Execution
    • Serve as the single accountable manager for all Task Order performance, owning delivery outcomes across cost, schedule, and performance baselines
    • Establish and maintain project governance, reporting cadences, and performance management processes in alignment with contractual and PWS requirements
    • Deliver Monthly Status Reports (MSR) covering all required content including activities vs. plan, personnel status, milestone tracking, CLIN projections, labor category hours, limitation of funds notices, and risk register updates
    • Convene re-occurring customer focused meetings with Government leadership
    • Maintain real-time visibility into cost, schedule, performance, and risk across all active task areas and team locations
    • Identify risks, issues, and dependencies and drive timely resolution with actionable mitigation strategies and documented corrective actions
    • Present program status, performance metrics, and decision options to customers through regular and on-demand briefings
  • Customer Engagement & Adoption
    • Serve as the primary contractor interface with the AAS COR and ASA-ALT TPOC on all contractual and performance matters
    • Demonstrate CCaR™ capabilities to customers and working-level users, clearly articulating mission and decision advantage
    • Facilitate stakeholder communications to maintain transparency, trust, and alignment with Government program authorities throughout performance
    • Support CCaR™ adoption efforts by coordinating user onboarding, addressing field-level concerns, and ensuring effective communication of system capabilities to working-level users and supporting organizations
  • Deployment & Implementation
    • Direct and coordinate cross-functional contractor teams operating across multiple locations
    • Oversee execution of all approved staffing plans and schedules
    • Oversee the deployment team responsible for:
      • Mapping existing financial processes to CCaR™ workflows
      • Configuring and implementing CCaR™ to meet mission and task order requirements
      • Supporting data integration efforts across Army financial systems
      • Delivering training to Army organizations, staff, and supporting stakeholders
    • Ensure successful onboarding of users across Army PAE organizations, tracking progress against approved schedules and milestones
  • Policy, Process, and Transformation
    • Advise leadership on policy updates, governance structures, and implementation memos to institutionalize CCaR™ usage
    • Support alignment to DoW and Army financial management policies
    • Drive standardization of budget and execution data, reporting, and analysis
    • Establish and support executive operating rhythms, including budget reviews, execution reviews, and budget drills
  • Product Feedback & Growth
    • Capture user feedback and operational insights to identify systemic performance trends and improvement opportunities
    • Identify team performance patterns and support continuous improvement of internal quality control and delivery processes
    • Collaborate with product and engineering teams to ensure field insights are translated into capabilities

Knowledge and Skills:

  • Proven experience managing complex, multi-stakeholder programs in a Government contracting environment with COR/TPOC accountability
  • Strong ability to engage and communicate effectively with Government customers, contracting officers, and senior program stakeholders
  • Demonstrated ability to lead and coordinate cross-functional teams operating across multiple locations and work arrangements
  • Strong skills in program planning, execution, risk management, deliverable tracking, and stakeholder coordination
  • Strong briefing and communication skills, with the ability to translate complex data into actionable insights
  • Experience managing contractual performance, quality assurance compliance, and delivering against defined scope, schedule, and cost baselines
  • Proficiency in producing Government-quality status reports, briefings, and formal correspondence
  • Experience with issue escalation, corrective action planning, and problem resolution
  • Comprehensive knowledge of DoW Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) process
  • Hands-on experience with defense business and accounting systems, including GFEBS or comparable systems
  • Strong understanding of QASP compliance, QM scoring, and performance-based contracting standards
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate operational data into clear decision-ready insights for Government leadership
  • Other, preferred qualifications:
    • Experience with enterprise financial management software deployments
    • Familiarity with data analytics, dashboards, and decision-support tools (e.g., Qlik, Power BI, or similar)
    • Understanding of system integrations across financial, contracting, and program management platforms in a defense environment
    • Prior experience with PMRT, CCaR™ or similar financial systems

Education and Work Experience:

  • This position requires a minimum of a Master’s degree from an accredited college or university in business management, engineering, computer science, economics or other related disciplines
  • A minimum of ten (10) years of experience in DoW program management, with a minimum of five (5) years of recent experience managing programs or supporting DoW financial within the last seven (7) years
  • Active Project Management Professional (PMP), Program Management Professional (PgMP), or equivalent project/program management certification from a recognized credentialing organization is required
  • Proven record of leading customer programs for complex, mission-critical software solutions within defense, federal, or enterprise environments

Physical & Mental Qualifications:

  • Must be able to sit, type, hear, see, and speak for extended periods of time
  • Must consistently work and type on a computer for prolonged periods of time
  • Must be able to able to communicate accurate information and ideas so others will understand
  • Must be able to lift/carry at least 15 lbs
  • May be required to move about inside an office to access file cabinets, office supplies, et.

Security Clearance:

  • Applicants selected for employment may/will be subject to a federal background investigation and must meet additional eligibility requirements for access to classified information or materials

Travel:

  • Some travel may be required

Hours:

  • Normal work schedule hours may vary, Monday through Friday. May be required to work additional hours and/or weekends, as needed, to meet deadlines or to fulfill travel obligations

Salary Range:

  • $160,000 - $180,000 per year
  • The estimated salary range listed is a good faith determination of potential base compensation that may be offered to a successful applicant for this position at the time of this job posting and may be modified in the future. The disclosed salary range estimate has not been adjusted for the applicable geographic differential associated with the location at which the position may be filled. When determining an applicant’s compensation, various factors are taken into consideration including, but not limited to: geographic location, relevant prior work experience, relevant training, special skills/competencies, education, clearance, licenses/certifications, labor categories/contract rates and other business needs.

IDS offers a robust benefits package including employer paid health, dental, vision, disability, AD&D and life insurance plans for eligible employees. IDS also offers a variety of elective plans to eligible employees including flexible spending accounts, voluntary life insurance and supplemental insurance plans. title: Security Analyst (Mid-Level) – w/active Top Secret clearance
description:
Overview

LMI is a new breed of digital solutions provider dedicated to accelerating government impact with innovation and speed. Investing in technology and prototypes ahead of need, LMI brings commercial-grade platforms and mission-ready AI to federal agencies at commercial speed.

Leveraging our mission-ready technology and solutions, proven expertise in federal deployment, and strategic relationships, we enhance outcomes for the government, efficiently and effectively. With a focus on agility and collaboration, LMI serves the defense, space, homeland, healthcare, and intelligence sectors—helping agencies navigate complexity and outpace change. Headquartered in Tysons, Virginia, LMI is committed to delivering impactful results that strengthen missions and drive lasting value.

Responsibilities

LMI is seeking a mission‑driven, detail‑oriented Security Analyst to support our Lead Facility Security Officer (FSO) across a large, multi‑site, clearance‑intensive federal program. This mid‑level role is ideal for an early‑career security professional with strong judgment, excellent communication skills, and experience working in classified environments, who is ready to take ownership of daily security operations while supporting complex personnel, physical, and industrial security requirements.

This position plays a critical part in maintaining compliance, accelerating clearance workflows, and ensuring a smooth and coordinated security posture across all program locations.

The Security Analyst serves as an essential extension of the Lead FSO, supporting the day‑to‑day administration of personnel security, access management, clearance verification, and facility compliance. This individual ensures candidates and employees move efficiently through LMI’s internal screening process before being submitted to customer review, and helps maintain security readiness across multiple sites with varied classification and SAP requirements.

The Security Analyst collaborates closely with recruiters, hiring managers, onboarding teams, subcontractor partners, and government security representatives to reinforce consistency, accuracy, and proactive issue identification across the program.

Key Responsibilities

Personnel Security & Clearance Management

  • Validate candidate clearance levels and eligibility as part of LMI’s internal pre‑screening workflow before any candidate is submitted to the customer.
  • Conduct initial clearance checks, reinvestigation status reviews, crossover feasibility assessments, and SAP eligibility evaluations.
  • Manage and track security documentation including e‑QIP initiation, SF‑86 updates, visit requests, and access rosters.
  • Support continuous monitoring of personnel security status, including periodic reinvestigations and onboarding compliance.
  • Prepare candidate security packages in alignment with program requirements and customer standards.

Program Screening & Candidate Workflow Support

  • Work closely with recruiters to review incoming candidate profiles for clearance accuracy and suitability.
  • Use LMI’s automated tracking tools to log, validate, and process new candidate submissions as part of the internal security review workflow.
  • Ensure candidate screening steps are completed rapidly and thoroughly, preventing delays in customer submission and nomination.
  • Flag discrepancies, risks, or incomplete information early and coordinate resolution with recruiters and hiring managers.

Support to Lead FSO & Multi‑Site Operations

  • Assist the Lead FSO with day‑to‑day administration of personnel security and classified facility operations.
  • Coordinate onboarding‑related access requirements, badging requests, clearance verification, and site‑specific access protocols with internal and government POCs.
  • Help maintain compliance with NISPOM, ICD 705, DoD/IC security requirements, and program‑specific customer guidance.
  • Support security reviews, audits, self‑inspections, and documentation updates across multiple program locations.
  • Provide ongoing support during facility visits, classified meetings, and high‑volume hiring periods.

Issue Identification & Operational Escalation

  • Monitor clearance processing timelines, candidate status changes, and workflow bottlenecks.
  • Identify emerging staffing or clearance challenges early and escalate them to the Lead FSO and Recruiting Manager.
  • Communicate security‑related risks, delays, market constraints, or clearance hurdles that may impact hiring timelines.
  • Support the Recruiting Manager in providing market‑driven insights to leadership, helping refine expectations, role requirements, and staffing approaches.
  • Contribute to cross-functional standups and alignment sessions to ensure real‑time visibility of security operations.

Qualifications

Required:

  • 2–5 years of experience in personnel security, industrial security, or classified program support.
  • Familiarity with TS/SCI clearance processes, adjudication workflows, reinvestigation requirements, and SAP eligibility fundamentals.
  • Experience with JPAS/DISS, e‑QIP, visit authorization requests, access rosters, and clearance documentation.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to manage sensitive information with discretion.
  • Proven ability to work in fast‑moving environments with high-volume candidate flow and rapidly evolving security requirements.
  • Excellent communication skills and ability to partner effectively with recruiters, hiring managers, subcontractor teammates, and government stakeholders.
  • Active TS/SCI clearance required; SAP eligibility strongly preferred.

TS/SCI clearance with SAP eligibility is required for this position. Applicants selected will be subject to a government security investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information. LMI will only consider applicants with current security clearances. Please note that only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance.

Target salary range: $50,000 - $100,000

title: Azure Data Engineer — Hybrid, Scalable Platform Expert
description:
PHP Professionals in Amsterdam zoekt een Data Engineer die het nieuwe dataplatform verder uitbouwt en zorgt voor performance- en kwaliteit. Je krijgt verantwoordelijkheid en vrijheid om mee te denken aan slimme toepassingen voor dataproducten, met een Agile team.

title: Data Engineer
description:
Ben jij die Data Engineer die graag werkt aan de kern van een dataplatform? Die het mooi vindt om ruwe data om te zetten naar betrouwbare, bruikbare informatie waar dashboards, analyses én AI-toepassingen op kunnen draaien? Dan zijn we op zoek naar jou.

We zoeken een Data Engineer die ons dataplatform verder uitbouwt en onderhoudt. Jij zorgt ervoor dat uiteenlopende databronnen, van API's en relationele databases tot bestanden en SaaS-systemen, samenkomen in een schaalbaar platform. Je ontsluit deze bronnen en zet ruwe data om naar betrouwbare Silver- en Gold-modellen volgens de Medallion-architectuur. Met slimme datamodellen, kwaliteitscontroles en automatisering zorg je dat collega's en klanten altijd kunnen rekenen op consistente en hoogwaardige informatie.

Wat ga je doen als Data Engineer?

Als Data Engineer bouw je aan de ruggengraat van onze BI-oplossingen. Je werkt in een multidisciplinair R&D-team aan robuuste dataproducten die klanten daadwerkelijk verder helpen.

  • Ontwerpen, ontwikkelen en onderhouden van schaalbare data pipelines en notebooks (o.a. in Databricks, Microsoft Fabric)
  • Realiseren van robuuste dataflows van bron tot verwerkbare dataset, met Python (PySpark), SQL en automation
  • Bouwen van generieke, herbruikbare oplossingen voor andere teams en klanten
  • Zorgen voor kwaliteit via testing, monitoring en versioning van data pipelines
  • Ontwerpen van datasets die direct geschikt zijn voor dashboards, analytische toepassingen én moderne features zoals Data Chat
  • Verkennen en toepassen van AI/ML-toepassingen in het dataplatform (bijv. via Databricks-integraties)
  • Documenteren van technische keuzes zodat overdraagbaarheid en onderhoud geborgd zijn
  • Werken volgens coding guidelines, definition of done en CI/CD-principes
  • Actieve deelname aan SCRUM-events en signaleren van verbeteringen op het vlak van performance en datakwaliteit

Waarom deze functie bij jou past

Je werkt op HBO/WO niveau en hebt een pragmatische, resultaatgerichte houding. Je hebt ervaring met Databricks (inclusief PySpark en notebooks), kennis van Microsoft Fabric en SQL. Je bent bekend met data engineering principes zoals ETL/ELT, orchestration en data modeling.

Je hebt affiniteit met CI/CD, monitoring en geautomatiseerd testen van data pipelines. Je begrijpt software engineering principes in een data-context: versiebeheer, modulariteit, herbruikbaarheid. Je bent ervaren met Agile werken (SCRUM) en samenwerken in multidisciplinaire teams.

Je kunt technische keuzes goed onderbouwen richting teamleden en bent nieuwsgierig, leergierig met een natuurlijke drang om te verbeteren. Je bent een teamspeler die eigenaarschap neemt voor de kwaliteit en continuïteit van data-oplossingen.

Interesse in (of ervaring met) AI/ML is een pre, binnen het R&D-team zijn er volop mogelijkheden om met innovatieve technologieën te experimenteren. Ook ervaring met het Azure-ecosysteem (Azure Data Lake, Azure DevOps, Terraform) of inzicht in de datastrategie van woningcorporaties is welkom, maar niet vereist.

Waarom werken bij Aareon?

Wij snappen dat een goede baan meer is dan alleen werk. Daarom krijg je bij ons:

  • Prestatiebeloning van maximaal twee maandsalarissen
  • Leaseauto van de zaak
  • 27 vakantiedagen (fulltime), met extra dagen bij 5 en 10 dienstjaren
  • Pensioenregeling bij ASR (80% betaald door Aareon)
  • Studiekostenvergoeding voor opleidingen en certificeringen
  • Hybride werken mogelijk, kantoor (Groningen of Breda), thuis en klantlocaties
  • Werkweek van 40 uur, deeltijd bespreekbaar (36 of 32 uur)
  • Bedrijfsfitness via Bedrijfsfitness Nederland met bijdrage van Aareon
  • Laptop en smartphone voor je werk

Bij Blue-Mountain en Aareon geloven we in diversiteit. Twijfel je of je aan alle eisen voldoet? We waarderen ervaring, maar ook drive en leervermogen. Iedereen is welkom.

Kennismakingsgesprek Een eerste gesprek om nader kennis te maken en te bepalen of we bij elkaar passen.

Uitwerken casus Je krijgt een korte casus om uit te werken zodat we een helder beeld krijgen van je capaciteiten.

Afrondend gesprek Ten slotte gaan we in detail in gesprek over de arbeidsvoorwaarden.

title: Associate Director of Government Relations
description:
The Position



Title : Associate Director of Government Relations

Position Type: Full time

Requisition No: 27007

Category : Management

Supervisor : Vice President of Government Relations

Last Updated : September 2026

Job Purpose : The Associate Director of Government Relations will support the work being led by the

government relations team.

Location: Hybrid, primary location in Sacramento with in-person work expected at various locations

throughout California

Salary Range: The beginning salary range for this position is Range M-18 (Steps 1-3) $137,586.46 -

$151,714.85



**The first review of the application shall occur approximately on 10/05/2026**


Position Overview


The Associate Director of Government Relations will support Calbright College’s government relations team, helping lead the development and execution of state advocacy strategies and legislative priorities that advance Calbright’s mission. This role combines strategic policy leadership with direct legislative advocacy, representing Calbright before the California Legislature, the Office of the Governor, regulatory agencies, and statewide coalitions. Under the direction of the Vice President of Government Relations, the Associate Director will help lead Calbright’s engagement on higher education in an effort to best position the College as a leading voice in competency-based education and short-term credentials policy landscape.


Essential Job Duties and Responsibilities


The duties below are representative of the role and are not intended to cover all of the duties performed within the scope of work.


  • Under the direction of the VIce President of Government Relations, manage the development, execution and evaluation of Calbright’s state advocacy strategy, including legislative priorities, regulatory engagement, and budget advocacy.
  • Monitor, analyze and report on state legislative, regulatory, and budget proposals related to higher education, workforce development and technology policy.
  • Update the Vice President of Government Relations on emerging policy threats and opportunities.
  • Anticipate legislative and regulatory developments and proactively position Calbright to shape policy outcomes.
  • Draft proposals for sponsored legislation and develop recommendations on amendments to proposed legislation.
  • Consult and support the development of opinion editorials, podcast and media appearances, panel opportunities and other initiatives in coordination with the Director of Communications and the Marketing and Communications team.
  • Develop and maintain a comprehensive legislative tracking and stakeholder mapping system to inform institutional strategy.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned that support the objective of the position.


Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities


  • Knowledge of the inner workings of California state government, including but not limited to the bodies of state government, the legislative process, the budget cycle, and the three public systems of higher education.
  • Knowledge of direct lobbying practices, legislative strategy development, and coalition management in Sacramento.
  • Experience working with contract lobbyists at state and federal levels.
  • Experience working on emergent higher education and workforce development policy issues, such as competency-based education, credit for prior learning, adult learners, skills-based hiring, and virtual learning environments.
  • Knowledge of general principles of systems change, collective impact, and process improvement.
  • Knowledge of project management best practices and principles.
  • Experience working with business applications including G Suite, Slack, video conferencing, and Asana.
  • Experience developing and executing advocacy strategies with minimal supervision, exercising sound political judgment in fast-moving legislative environments.
  • Experience building and maintaining productive working relationships with elected officials, legislative staff, regulatory agency officials and staff, and coalition partners in a bipartisan manner.
  • Prioritize equity in education and economic opportunity for historically underrepresented groups in California.
  • Communicate in a professional and concise manner, orally and in writing, in both informal and formal settings, including but not limited to written and oral testimony, presentations and direct lobbying meetings.
  • Organize and prioritize work, manage time, and meet deadlines via self-directed project management.
  • Ability to problem-solve by quickly assessing issues and opportunities and using sound judgment to determine appropriate courses of action, associated timelines, and key collaborators.
  • Work independently and collaboratively depending on the nature of the assignment.
  • Manage multiple projects, assignments, and stakeholder relationships simultaneously with the judgment to prioritize deadlines.
  • Read, analyze, and synthesize complex legislative, regulatory, and budget documents for personal and shared use.
  • Ability to regularly prepare written memos to executive leadership.
  • Demonstrate understanding of, sensitivity to, and respect for the diverse academic, socio-economic, ethnic, religious, and cultural backgrounds, disability, and sexual orientation of community college students, staff and faculty.


Minimum Qualifications

Calbright College provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, age, veteran status, disability or genetics. Who We Are

Calbright College is one of California’s newest community colleges – the first statewide, online campus designed to bridge the gap between employers with unfilled positions and students who don’t have either the time or money to attend a traditional school. title: Casual Line Cooks

This hands-on position is responsible for preparing and serving concession-style food items while maintaining food safety, quality, and efficiency standards. title: CRIMINAL JUSTICE TRAINER 4 - Basic Training Division
description:
Description

The duty station for this position is in King County, therefore the incumbent will receive 5% premium pay in addition to the salary listed above.

The Opportunity:

The Washington State Criminal Justice Training Commission (WSCJTC) is seeking an expert level law enforcement training professional to provide leadership, mentorship, and guidance to Criminal Justice Trainers within the Basic Training Division (BTD). This Criminal Justice Trainer 4, will provide expert level training while also serving as a supervisor to senior level trainers. The incumbent will serve a vital role in developing and supporting the trainers responsible for preparing Washington’s newest law enforcement officers with the knowledge and skills to safely protect the communities they serve.

If you are an expert level law enforcement trainer who is passionate about developing others, strengthening instructional excellence, and helping prepare both trainers and future law enforcement officers for success, we encourage you to apply!

The Benefits: WSCJTC offers outstanding healthcare benefits, choice of state retirement programs including a defined benefit pension plan, advancement opportunities, and flexible/compressed work schedules.

At the WSCJTC, we value the importance of creating an environment in which all employees feel respected, included, and empowered to bring unique ideas to the agency. Our diversity and inclusion efforts include embracing different cultures, backgrounds, and perspectives while fostering growth and advancement in the workplace.

Duties

Duties assigned to this position include (but are not limited to):

  • Supervise Criminal Justice Trainers and lead by example, guided by the agency values, and encourage staff to do the same.
  • Reinforce, demonstrate, and model ethical, professional, and trustworthy behavior to support the ideal of public servants who earn the trust of their communities.
  • Ensure staff are adequately trained and kept abreast of best practices, current case law, and agency curriculum to effectively deliver training.
  • Ensure that work conducted by staff is accomplished in accordance with RCW/WAC/State Rules/Agency Policies and Curriculum.
  • Evaluate, develop, correct, and mentor staff on their work performance, including providing guidelines and performance feedback.
  • Facilitate instruction, including classroom, practical, and mock scenarios.
  • Serve as a TAC Officer of BLEA classes, as needed.
  • Train and mentor students guided by CJTC policy, rules, and regulations, and the agency values.
  • Maintain order within the academy atmosphere, including motivating classes as a group and students individually in accordance with any policy.
  • Perform inspections, drill protocols, and ceremonies.
  • Communicate with students’ employing agencies regarding performance, attendance, coordination of additional training needs, test failures and remedial training, if needed.
  • Serve as SME on current law enforcement curriculum in high-risk patrol procedures and other areas, in accordance with knowledge and experience, and when curricular updates are required.
  • Liaise with internal and external partners to ensure curriculum meets agency standards and industry best practices.
  • Chair or serve on workgroups within areas of expertise, ensuring the Basic Training perspective is considered as projects, programs, or curriculum are developed or updated.
  • Serve as an ad hoc member of the Risk Roundtable Committee.
  • Upon request by or with assistance of the Agency Risk Manager, Certification Bureau, or Records Manager, act as a subject matter expert in identifying appropriate curriculum records and serving as an expert witness regarding the content of curriculum delivered in high-risk disciplines, patrol procedures, and other areas as directed.

Qualifications

  • Required Qualifications/Experience:

  • At least seven (7) years of experience in law enforcement or related military assignments that may require the application of physical force.
AND
  • At least three (3) years of experience training law enforcement personnel with the WSCJTC or within a criminal justice agency specifically in the areas of de-escalation, communication, criminal law, firearms, control/defensive tactics, and/or patrol procedures.
AND
  • At least two (2) years of experience leading or supervising law enforcement personnel. Time serving as a lead trainer/primary coach/TAC Officer/FTO or PTO are acceptable.
OR
  • A bachelor’s degree in criminal justice, public administration, sociology, psychology, adult education, forensics, or related field of study.
AND
  • At least five (5) years of experience in law enforcement or related military assignments that may require the application of physical force.
AS WELL AS:
  • An understanding of adult teaching and learning methods.
  • Ability to report information clearly, completely, and accurately both verbally and in writing.
  • No sustained use of force complaints in the past three (3) years.
  • Any community complaints in the last three (3) years must be satisfactorily explained.
  • Able to model the Guardian Philosophy of policing in class on a daily basis.
  • Strong work ethic, self-directed, and able to work in a team-teaching environment.
  • Ability to support the agency's diversity, equity, and inclusion goals.
  • Effective communication skills.
  • Problem-solving skills, including analysis and strategies.
  • Knowledge of training and instruction principles, content, and methodology.
  • Knowledge of curriculum development.
  • Knowledge of the criminal justice system, including federal, state, and local criminal justice agencies, laws, ordinances, and regulations.
  • Knowledge of cultural diversity/implicit bias.
  • Skills for basic computer applications, including Microsoft Office Suite.
  • The ability to take action to learn and grow.
  • The ability to take action to meet the needs of others.

Preferred/Desired Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in criminal justice, public administration, education, communications, sociology, psychology or related field of study.
  • Understanding of and/or experience with WSCJTC protocols and chain of command.
  • Experience with curriculum in the subject areas of de-escalation, patrol tactics, criminal procedures, less lethal weapons, firearms, and/or control/defensive tactics.
  • First-level supervisory experience (examples: sergeant, supervisor, manager).
  • Demonstrated experience controlling/monitoring equipment and resources.
  • WSCJTC Instructor Development - 2 (ID2) certification.
  • Program or project management.
  • Service on a multi-disciplinary or multi-agency task force, board, or commission.

Conditions of Employment:

  • Successfully complete the WSCJTC’s First Level Supervision course.

  • Successfully complete the WSCJTC’s Patrol Tactics Instructor (PTI) or Instructor Development course.

  • Attend and/or audit all BLEA course instruction modules.

  • Achieve BLEA Instructor Certification.

Supplemental Information

How to Apply:

Applications for this recruitment will be accepted electronically through NeoGov. Simply click the green "Apply" button in the upper right-hand corner to get started. Please attach the following to your online application:

  • A chronological Resume outlining your experience to date.
  • A Letter of Interest detailing your qualifications, and why you believe you are the best person for this role, and
  • A minimum of three (3) professional references who can attest to your work performance, technical skills, knowledge base, and job-related competencies.

We are looking for evidence in your application materials that you have the experience, skills, and abilities indicated in this job posting. Qualified applicants whose responses most closely match the requirements of this position may be invited to an interview. Carefully review your application before submitting. All information may be verified, and documentation may be required.

The initial screening will be solely based on the contents and completeness of the application materials submitted.

Applications from this posting may be used for up to 60 days to fill additional vacancies.

Veteran's Preference:

Applicants who meet the required qualifications for the position and wish to claim Veteran's Preference MUST attach a copy of their DD214, or other verification of military service. Please blackout any personally identifiable data such as social security numbers. For additional information on Veteran's Preference and guidance on how to determine if you are eligible, click here.

We thank you and are grateful for your service!

Contact Us:

If you have questions, contact Human Resources at humanresources@cjtc.wa.gov.

WSCJTC is an equal opportunity employer. Women, racial and ethnic minorities, persons of disability, persons over 40 years of age, disabled and Vietnam era veterans, and people of all sexual orientations and gender identities are encouraged to apply. Persons with disabilities needing assistance in the application process, or those needing this job announcement in an alternative format may contact the listed recruiter. title: Data Engineer
description:
Data sits at the heart of every digital product, analytics workflow, and AI initiative. As companies push more of these capabilities into production, the integrations that move and expose that data need to be solid. Datashift is looking for a Data Engineer to build and own those integrations.

Do you have strong Python skills, a genuine DevOps mindset, and a track record of shipping things that hold up in production? Do you feel at home across software engineering, data engineering, and operations?

You’re a practical engineer who takes pride in what ends up running in production. You care about reliability, security, and building APIs that other teams can count on.

Responsibilities

Own the full lifecycle of Data Integration. Build them in Python with Databricks, Azure Function Apps, and other Azure services, translating requirements into clean, maintainable code;

Keep APIs production ready. Performance, security, access control, observability, and cost all fall in your scope;

Move legacy data APIs onto the platform’s current architectural standards and add structured logging and alerting so issues surface before users notice them;

Own the CI/CD setup in Azure DevOps. Build pipelines that carry code through testing and deployment without manual steps;

Work with the Data Engineering & Platform team and engineers across teams and countries to shape, ship, and document integrations end to end;

Support the team with data engineering tasks where needed.

Job requirements

Qualifications

At least 3 years of Python experience and a track record of shipping APIs and backend services. Clean, testable code is your default.

You have real dbt experience and use it to build well-structured, maintainable data models. SQL is a given.

You know your way around API design, CI/CD pipelines, and testing. Keeping production systems observable and stable is something you have done before.

Azure is familiar ground. You have worked with Function Apps, Key Vault, VNets, private endpoints, NSGs, and secure API exposure in production.

Comfortable in an Agile setup, working daily with data engineers, platform engineers, and business stakeholders.

An interest in what is coming on the Databricks platform, particularly Lakebase and Databricks Apps.

Why join Datashift in the Netherlands?

Opportunity for strategic impact – Join a fast-growing data consultancy team, expand your skills, and work with top-tier organizations as clients—all while benefiting from the expertise and support of our established practice in Belgium.

Competitive package – Receive a comprehensive compensation & benefits plan tailored to match your experience and potential.

Award-winning workplace – We are based in CIC Rotterdam (one of Europe’s Leading Start-up Hubs according to the Financial Times), home to 150+ young companies and literally next to the iconic Centraal Station. A great commute guaranteed.

title: Independent Living Skills Instructor (Part-time)
description:
ILS Instructor/ Life Skills Coach

Young Adult Transition Program

Job Type: Part-time

Hours: 15 hours per week

Pay: $18–$20 per hour

Work Location: In person


Are You Looking for a Role Where You Teach Daily Living Skills and Support Students Toward Greater Independence?


College Living Experience (CLE) is a comprehensive post-secondary transition program supporting young adults diagnosed with autism, AD/HD, and learning differences. Students receive individualized support across academics, career development, social skills, and independent living while learning to manage adult responsibilities in real-world environments.

The Independent Living Skills (ILS) Instructor is responsible for supporting students’ development of essential daily living skills. This role focuses on assessing student functioning levels and providing direct instruction across all independent living domains, including health, safety, hygiene, food management, money management, housekeeping, housing, transportation, community integration, legal rights, interpersonal skills, and job-related life skills.

This position includes both individual and small-group instruction and requires consistent documentation, collaboration, and hands-on coaching.



This role is ideal for someone who enjoys working directly with young adults and teaching practical skills that support independence. One day, you may be coaching a student on household organization or meal planning. Another day, you may be leading a cooking group, supporting medication organization, or helping a student practice community safety skill. Over time, your instruction helps students gain confidence, self-reliance, and independence in daily life. Your work directly impacts students’ ability to live more independently and safely.


Why People Love Working at CLE

Working at CLE means being part of a collaborative, mission-driven team focused on meaningful student outcomes.

  • You see real progress. Students gain independence through consistent instruction and practice.
  • Your work is hands-on. Instructions happen where skills are actually used — homes and communities.
  • You’re supported by a team. Staff collaborate regularly to problem-solve and refine support.
  • Every day is different. Instruction spans many areas of daily living and community participation.

What You’ll Do

Independent Living Skills Instruction

  • Assist the ILS Coordinator or supervisor in completing CLE Independent Living Skills Inventories to assess student functioning across domains
  • Provide consistent, individualized instruction tailored to student needs and learning styles
  • Teach students individually and in small groups how to clean and maintain all aspects of their living spaces, including kitchens, bathrooms, bedrooms, and common areas
  • Lead small-group cooking classes, teaching a range of simple to complex recipes and modeling safe kitchen tool use
  • Assist students with weekly meal planning and grocery list development
  • Model appropriate hygiene and support instruction related to personal appearance and self-care
  • Instruct small groups on health, hygiene, fitness, transportation, safety, and community awareness

Medication Support

  • Visually verify that student medication is organized in weekly medication planners
  • Verbally verify with students that medication routines are being followed
  • Assist with medication refill coordination when appropriate, in collaboration with the ILS Coordinator or Director of Psychological Services

Learning Environment & Student Support

  • Manage the learning environment by reducing distractions that interfere with student focus
  • Adapt instruction as needed to support student engagement and understanding
  • Address student needs proactively and collaborate with team members to problem-solve concerns

Documentation & Team Collaboration

  • Complete documentation of instructional sessions and student progress in CLE systems within required timeframes
  • Report questions or concerns to the ILS Coordinator or supervisor promptly
  • Actively participate in weekly or bi-weekly staff meetings, training, and curriculum development
  • Participate in additional projects or initiatives as assigned

Who Thrives in This Role

  • This role is a strong fit for individuals who enjoy teaching practical skills, working in community-based settings, and supporting students through hands-on learning.
  • Successful ILS Instructors are patient, organized, observant, and able to balance structure with flexibility while promoting independence.

What Makes This Role Unique

  • You teach skills that directly impact daily independence
  • You work with students in real-world living environments
  • You provide both individualized and group instruction
  • You collaborate closely with a multidisciplinary support team

Benefits Include:

CLE offers a supportive work environment and benefits for eligible employees, which may include:

  • Health insurance
  • Dental insurance
  • Vision insurance
  • Health savings account (HSA)
  • Flexible spending account (FSA)
  • Life insurance
  • 401(k)
  • Paid time off

title: Sr. Project Manager - Organizational Change Management (OCM), Compliance, & Continuous Improvement
description:
About the Organization

E2 Consulting Engineers, LP (E2) is a professional services firm established in 1988 specializing in a full spectrum of engineering services including, project engineering and design, federal base operations and infrastructure support services, gas pipeline construction and inspection services, environmental consulting and remediation, and information technology services. At E2, we value safety, innovation and collaboration, and we are dedicated to excellence.

Overview

The Project Manager, Organizational Change Management (OCM), Compliance & Continuous Improvement, serves as the integration point between project management, change management, compliance improvement, and operational excellence functions within Gas Operations. This role leads cross-functional initiatives focused on Organizational Change Management (OCM), Management of Change (MOC), compliance improvement, audit findings remediation, process standardization, and operational transformation efforts across Gas Distribution and Gas Transmission. The position partners closely with Gas Compliance, Operations, Safety, IT, Training, PMO, and business leaders to drive sustainable improvements that strengthen regulatory compliance, operational effectiveness, employee adoption, and organizational readiness for change. The successful candidate will provide end-to-end project leadership while applying change management and continuous improvement methodologies to address complex operational challenges, improve compliance performance, and support strategic business objectives. This role requires strong project management, stakeholder engagement, facilitation, governance, analytical, and process improvement experience in a utility, regulated, or operational environment.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities

Project & Program Management

  • Lead multiple concurrent compliance, operational excellence, and process improvement initiatives across Gas Operations.

Organizational Change Management (OCM)

  • Develop and execute change management strategies for operational, process, technology, and compliance-related initiatives.
  • Conduct stakeholder analyses, change impact assessments, and organizational readiness evaluations.
  • Create and implement communication, engagement, training, and sustainment plans.
  • Partner with leaders to strengthen sponsorship and organizational commitment to change.

  • Identify and proactively manage change resistance and adoption risks.
  • Measure adoption, effectiveness, readiness, and sustainment of implemented changes.
  • Track benefits realization and ensure intended business outcomes are achieved.

Management of Change (MOC)

  • Support the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of Management of Change processes and governance practices.
  • Ensure operational, procedural, technological, and organizational changes are appropriately documented, reviewed, assessed, approved, and communicated.
  • Coordinate cross-functional reviews and implementation planning activities.
  • Facilitate alignment between MOC requirements, compliance obligations, training activities, and operational execution.
  • Support process standardization efforts that reduce risk and improve consistency across Gas Operations.

Compliance & Audit Findings Management

  • Partner with Gas Compliance and Operations leaders to track, prioritize, and resolve audit findings.
  • Develop remediation plans and monitor corrective actions through closure.
  • Identify systemic issues and recommend sustainable process improvements.
  • Support internal audits, regulatory reviews, and compliance assessments.

Continuous Improvement & Process Optimization

  • Facilitate process mapping, root cause analysis, future-state design, and continuous improvement workshops.
  • Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency, compliance, quality, customer outcomes, and employee experience.
  • Apply Lean, Six Sigma, Continuous Improvement, and problem-solving methodologies to improve business performance.
  • Develop and maintain standardized operating procedures, process documentation, workflows, and work instructions.
  • Support implementation and sustainment of process improvements across operational teams.
  • Monitor benefits realization and value delivery associated with improvement initiatives.

Governance & Risk Management

  • Maintain project controls, governance documentation, decision logs, and issue management processes.
  • Support governance boards and leadership forums through effective reporting and decision support materials.
  • Assess project, operational, compliance, and adoption risks and develop mitigation strategies.
  • Ensure quality assurance practices and documentation standards are consistently followed.
  • Promote accountability through structured governance, reporting, and continuous monitoring processes.
  • Stakeholder & Executive Engagement
  • Build strong partnerships across Gas Distribution, Gas Transmission, Compliance, Safety, Training, IT, PMO, and Leadership teams.
  • Facilitate workshops, working sessions, and stakeholder alignment meetings.
  • Present recommendations, risks, project progress, performance insights, and outcomes to various levels of leadership.
  • Facilitate consensus among diverse stakeholder groups and navigate competing priorities.
  • Foster collaboration and effective communication across cross-functional teams.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Operations Management, Organizational Development, Project Management, Communications, or a related field.
  • Minimum 5 years of experience leading cross-functional projects, programs, or business improvement initiatives.
  • Experience in project management, organizational change management, compliance programs, process improvement, or operational excellence initiatives.
  • Experience working within regulated, operational, utility, energy, manufacturing, transportation, or related environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex initiatives involving diverse stakeholder groups.
  • Strong facilitation, communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Experience developing executive presentations, status reports, dashboards, and business recommendations.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and collaboration tools.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.

Benefits

AI is transforming the world – and we’re just getting started. With data growing exponentially, the need for smart, impact-driven minds has never been greater. At Rewire, we don’t just follow trends in Data & AI – we shape them.

Collaborate with cross-functional teams from both the client and Rewire – contribute from day one while learning from experienced leaders

Join a vibrant, multidisciplinary team that’s ambitious, collaborative, and just the right amount of nerdy – where learning and laughter go hand in hand

Thrive in a culture that values autonomy, curiosity, and bold thinking – where your voice matters, ideas turn into action, and your impact is genuinely recognized and rewarded

When not onsite with clients, you’re warmly welcome to work from our Amsterdam office or from home. Rewire’s Amsterdam office is more than just a building – it’s a space designed to foster problem‑solving, collaboration, innovation, and, simply put, where we build the future.

Discover more about its inspiring atmospherehere .

“What I really enjoy about my job at Rewire is us being involved from the beginning to the end of implementing complex and innovative AI solutions. Secondly, working with the people here is simply a great deal of fun.” – Jacco Broere, Data Engineer at Rewire

Sound like your kind of team?

Perfect! If you’re ready to kick‑start your career and want to make real impact with data & AI, we’d love to hear from you.

We welcome all applicants – regardless of gender, background, or LGBT+ identity – because diversity and inclusion are core values for us. We are convinced that a diverse and inclusive workplace fosters creativity, innovation, and success.
